name: Drexaline
description: Drexaline is a synthetic catecholamine cascade accelerant that floods the bloodstream with a precisely titrated mixture of epinephrine analogues and norepinephrine amplifiers. Developed for Lazarus's corporate security division, it produces a controlled adrenal surge lasting 18-22 minutes, dramatically increasing strength output, vascular response, and pain threshold. The comedown is severe but survivable — the drug was engineered with liability in mind.
effects: Heart rate and cardiac output surge
Enhanced coagulation response to minor wounds
side_effects: Tunnel vision can cause missed threats
Vascular rupture risk in unaugmented users
cultural_context: Drexaline is the respectable face of combat pharmacology — corporate security teams, licensed bodyguards, and Tier 3 fixers who can afford a prescription use it openly. On the Shelf it's called 'The Flood' and is considered a step up from crude street stims, a sign that a runner has connections. Tier 4 executives sometimes keep a pen in their desk 'just in case.'
story_hooks: A Tier 3 runner survives a hit because their Drexaline pen was medical-grade — then learns the batch was recalled for a cardiac defect affecting 1 in 400 users, and they've already used two doses
Lazarus is quietly buying back street-circulating Drexaline from a diverted corporate shipment — the person selling it doesn't know why the corp wants it back so badly
A bodyguard on Drexaline kills someone they shouldn't have during a tunnel-vision episode; now both the corp and the victim's family want answers
related_entities: Ouroboros Energy ThermalSink UR-3 District Waste Heat Exchange Network
